summary:
{
  "ledger": [
    "Wooden table | Diagonal tabletop fills foreground and extends toward upper right; child stands beyond its left/far edge | Same tabletop surrounds bowl in tighter framing | Grain, seams and edges remain compatible as the camera widens briefly and then moves closer; table occludes the child's lower body.",
    "Glass bowl | On tabletop in front of child and left of small metal cup; opening viewed from above | Remains on table in close-up | Near rim stays in front of contents; transparent walls permit views of balls, fingers and wood beneath without an opaque-surface contradiction.",
    "Small metal cup | On tabletop to the right of the glass bowl | Outside the final close-up | Maintains its rightward position while visible and leaves the image as framing tightens.",
    "Loose tabletop balls | At the right edge of the table image, farther right and nearer the camera than the metal cup | Outside the final close-up | Wider framing reveals more of this cluster; tighter framing crops it without a demonstrated layout change.",
    "Child and moving hands | Child behind bowl on far-left side of table; hands approach bowl from above | Child remains behind bowl while one hand moves among its contents and the other stays near the far-right rim | Hands occlude balls behind them; balls reappear around the moving hand without a clear wrong-side emergence or depth-order reversal.",
    "Balls inside bowl | Clustered below the bowl opening | Moving around the bowl interior | Their projected positions and overlaps change during handling; visibility through the glass and temporary occlusion by hands remain geometrically plausible.",
    "Patio and background fixtures | Paving surrounds table; wider views reveal pots and a leaning white rectangular frame beyond it at upper right | Background mostly cropped from close-up | Background remains behind child and table; no traversed doorway or room connection is shown.",
    "Camera viewpoint | Elevated oblique view across bowl toward child | Tighter elevated view of bowl and hands from the same side | Brief widening reveals more patio and tabletop before progressive tightening; no cut or reversal requires an incompatible scene map."
  ],
  "findings": []
}
